Compendium

kuhm-PEN-dee-uhm · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Compendium is a detailed collection or summary of information on a subject.

Every camp counselor was handed a battered compendium of first-aid procedures before the first hike of the summer.

Worked Example

Rather than search a dozen separate cookbooks, the chef finally assembled her own compendium of family recipes, organized by decade.

A compendium gathers scattered information into one thorough, organized reference.

How Compendium Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

anthology

anthology: a published collection of works or information

digest

digest: a condensed collection of information

Antonyms

fragment

fragment: a small, incomplete piece of something

snippet

snippet: a tiny, isolated piece of information

How Strong Is It? — list → encyclopedia → compendium

list vs. compendium

list vs. compendium: A list is just a simple, often unorganized set of items, without the thorough detail a true compendium provides.

encyclopedia vs. compendium

encyclopedia vs. compendium: An encyclopedia goes further than a compendium, aiming to cover an entire field exhaustively rather than a single, focused subject.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of compendium.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — com-

prefix — com-: with, together (before b, m, p) (Latin)

root — pend-

root — pend-: to weigh, to hang (Latin pendere)

suffix — -ium

suffix — -ium: Latin noun ending (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Compendium comes from Latin com- ('together') plus pendere ('to weigh') and the noun ending -ium -- originally 'that which is weighed together,' a well-organized summary. The same root gives English the everyday word depend.

Use the root in a new word: depend

Use the root in a new word: depend: The entire hiking trip depends on tomorrow's weather forecast.

Word Choice

Compendium always implies real thoroughness -- it's a compliment to call a reference book a compendium, since it suggests the author gathered and organized a great deal of scattered information.
